The **Menu knowledge** screen is where you sit down and fill in the notes
that the diner-facing assistant reads about your venue. It's the same
data the Hub's openers count and the same the assistant leans on when it
answers a guest — so nothing here can quietly disagree with either.

Direct URL: `rumizi.com/your-venue/w/knowledge`.

## What's on it

The page opens on **Guests asked** — the worklist of what a guest
put to the assistant that it had nothing to go on for. Each row names
the dish, the field the answer needed (ingredients, allergens, or how
it's served and portioned), and how many guests have asked. Answer once
and the row goes; a vendor who fills the column in the menu editor
never sees it either. Nothing is stored as a gap — the row is open only
while the field is still empty on the live dish.

Below that, four groups in the same worklist model:

- **About the venue** — one paragraph the assistant uses for anything a
  guest might ask that isn't on the menu. Parking, allergies you handle
  carefully, what you're known for. Edit it in **Settings** if you'd
  rather.
- **Dishes** — one line per dish. **Diners read these on the menu card**,
  so write them the way you'd speak to a guest.
- **Sections** — a short note per category. Read only by the assistant.
- **Menus** — a short note per menu. Read only by the assistant.

The counter at the top of each group reads *"3 of 12 described"*, so
progress is visible at a glance while you work down a long menu.

<Note>
A row disappears from the list the moment you save it. The list is
**what's still missing**, and the counts moving with it are the only
signal you get that you're closing gaps.
</Note>

## Who sees the notes

| Note | Read by the guest assistant | Printed on the menu card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Venue** | Yes | No |
| **Menu** | Yes | No |
| **Section** | Yes | No |
| **Dish** | Yes | Yes |

Dish notes are also translated into every language you offer, so a
guest reading in French sees the note in French. Venue, menu, and
section notes are sent to the assistant as written.

Hidden items don't count — the assistant doesn't recommend what a
guest can't see, so filling in a note for a hidden dish is work for
nobody. The screen calls them out under the counter so you know why
the totals differ from your menu editor.

## When the screen isn't there

The knowledge screen is only visible when the **diner-facing menu
assistant** is on for your venue — Pro AI or Max AI, and not disabled
by request. A venue whose guests have no assistant would be writing
for nobody. See [Plans and billing](/vendors/billing/subscription).
